How to Submit Public Comment:
Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of the following
methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit it to the City Clerk
prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes per person per item. At the Chair’ s
discretion, the time limit may be shortened to allow all speakers to address the Community Services
Commission.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website as noted below. Public
Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting day will be forwarded to the Commission
before the meeting for their consideration but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted
after 4:00 P.M. will be forwarded to Commission but may not be received before the meeting.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at Public Comment.

Watch the Meeting Online

   MINUTES OF MAY 4, 2026
 REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION

CALL TO ORDER

Vice Chair Rodriguez called the regular meeting of the Community Services Commission to
order at 6:36 P.M. on Monday, May 4, 2026, with Commissioners and staff in the Council
Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Youth Ambassador Fang.

ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Nancy Duong, Mary Huang, Darwin Rodriguez

Commissioners Absent:  Davis Barrantes

Youth Ambassadors Present:  Amy Perez, Jiayi Fang

ANNOUNCEMENTS
Assistant Director Morales-Stevens provided information for the public on how to submit
comments and how to request meeting agendas. If you wish to address the Community Services
Commission, email all public comments to CSCommission@sangabriel.gov.

1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

The agenda was approved.

2. PUBLIC COMMENT
  None.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  MAY 4, 2026
 3. ACTION ITEMS

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A motion was made by Commissioner Duong and seconded by Commissioner Huang
  to approve the minutes of the Community Services Commission Meeting for April 6,
  2026.

  Motion approved as presented by a vote of 3-0- as follows:

  AYES:  DUONG, HUANG, RODRIGUEZ
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  BARRANTES

4. DISCUSSION ITEMS

  A. EVENTS AND PROGRAMS UPDATES
  Presented by Recreation Supervisor Shoup

  The Commission asked about pool party rates and any updates to Recreation Swim or
  charging processes, noting credit card delays.

  They also inquired about private swim lessons, registration, and city profits from swim
  classes.

  Additionally, they questioned how the Summer in San Gabriel Series will be promoted
  beyond social media and requested data on social media post analytics, they are seeking
  information from the PIO.

  B. DISCUSSION OF WORKPLAN
  Presented by Vice Chair Rodriguez

  The Commission aims to launch a survey quickly to capture website traffic during summer
  programming. They thanked youth ambassadors for their feedback on engaging students,
  suggesting interactive social media posts and study sessions at local cafes.

  They discussed the RIDESG program and recommended marketing programs at local
  businesses and supermarkets. They are hopeful of targeting more ethnic audiences. Youth
  ambassadors recommended using Parent Square for communication and commission
  requested contacting local schools to distribute program and event flyers. The
  Commission stated they would like to invite the PIO to attend a future meeting to discuss
  marketing reach.

COMMUNITY SERVICES COMMISSION REGULAR MEETING MINUTES  MAY 4, 2026
 5. COMMISSIONER REPORTS

  Commissioner Huang shared there was a donation of new benches at Smith Park.

  Vice Chair Rodriguez enjoyed the San Gabriel Farmer’s Market.

6. STAFF COMMENTS
  Presented by Assistant Director Morales-Stevens

  The Youth Ambassadors, Commissioner Huang and Vice Chair Rodriguez shared some words
  regarding their final meetings.

7. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular meeting held on Monday, June 1, 2026, in the Council Chamber at City

  STAFF REPORT
DATE:  June 1, 2026

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

BY:  Ana Casillas, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Cinco De Mayo Recap

The Community Services Department held its annual Cinco De Mayo Mercado event on
Friday, May 1 from 5:30 p.m. to 9:00 p.m. at the San Gabriel Mission District. The event
featured a variety of artisan vendors, food trucks, beer and specialty drink area,
community booths, kid’s activities, grito contest and live entertainment.

Entertainment performances started at 5:45p.m. on an outdoor stage with a lineup of
Ballet de Sally Savedra Ballet Folklorico group, Los Pollos and Pollitos youth mariachi
groups, and concluded with Mariachi Garibaldi de Jaime Cueller. New features this year
were a Roping Challenge booth, Loteria games in the Padillo Room, and an inflatable
obstacle course.

All the new elements were very well received. Staff would like to continue expanding the
newly added elements by extending the time for Loteria and adding another new element
next year to attract an even bigger turnout.
   City of San Gabriel
  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  June 1, 2026

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

BY:  Andy Shoup, Recreation Supervisor

SUBJECT:  Recap of Play Day - 2026

The Community Services Department held the 61st Annual Play Day event on Saturday,
May 16, 2026, from 11am to 2pm, at the La Laguna Playground of Vincent Lugo Park.
Building on the success of last year, nearly 500 residents were in attendance. The patrons
enjoyed the park, along with music, crafts, games, face painting, balloon twisters, and
activities provided by 11 community groups. The Tacos La Dona food truck, and Sungold
Ice Pops were also on-site, serving lunch and refreshments for the event.

Looking ahead to the 2027 event, to be held on Saturday, May 15. Staff will work to
increase participation, add additional activities, as well as a revised layout designed to
bring more participants to the La Laguna playground. Staff will also determine ways to
reduce wait times for the face painting and balloon twister lines.

  MEMORANDUM
DATE:  June 1, 2026

TO:  Community Services Commission

FROM:  Matthew Morales-Stevens, Community Services Assistant Director

SUBJECT:  Community Services Commission Workplan

SUMMARY
The Community Services Commission approved the most recent workplan at the October
7, 2024 commission meeting the Community Services Commission decided to change it
from an annual workplan to an ongoing document that can be adjusted if and when
needed to better address the needs of the department. The Commission has been making
incremental changes since the last approval.

PURPOSE OF THE COMMISSION
The purpose of the Community Services Commission is to creatively and inclusively
explore ways in which the Community Services Department can enrich quality of life for
residents of the City of San Gabriel by providing equitable access to dynamic programs,
services and spaces that strengthen community connection and engagement.

SCOPE OF THE COMMISSION
The Community Services Commission serves as an advisory body to the Community
Services Department and City Council, and functions as a liaison between residents and
city government. It is the responsibility of the Community Services Commission to
advocate on behalf of the San Gabriel community and to ensure that the Community
Services Department’s programs, services, spaces and events advance the Commission’s
purpose.

Purpose of the Workplan
The Annual Workplan is intended to guide the work of the Community Services
Commission and outline the areas of focus for 2024. It includes proposed programs and
projects that will be implemented and completed throughout the year.
 Current Workplan
The workplan sets four priority areas as identified in the Community Services
Strategic Plan for the Community Services Department. The following list of ideas,
programs and activities are not intended to be exhaustive or to limit the action items the
Commission can explore. The list below reflects amendments made at the July and
October Regular Community Services Commission Meetings.

  1. Create New Innovative Programs and Services to Engage the Entire
  Community
  a. Provide programs for residents with the age groups, 13-18 and 30-50.
  b. Explore program offerings for persons with disabilities including but not
  limited to swim classes.
  c. Continue the youth ambassador program for the Community Services
  Commission
  d. Optimizing participation- Gaining residents vs non-residents

  2. Connect the Entire Community to Enhance Quality of Life
  a. Connect all geographic areas of the City
  i. Examples include: Hosting events and programs in the South San
  Gabriel area and various other neighborhoods such as a tiny tots
  soccer class at Marshall Park or a partnership with the Garvey School
  District.
  ii. Introduction of contract class soccer lessons at Marshall Park
  b. Host resource fair at Marshall Park.

  3. Develop Innovative Resources and Tools to Achieve our Mission
  a. Modify resident survey and collect data with targeted questions to
  improve and enhance programs, events and services.
Next Steps:
  1. Explore challenger baseball- adaptive sports
  2. Explore Very Important Person Soccer- adaptive sports
  3. Develop new Bike event at a local park
  a. Contact stakeholders and secure a date
